title: Fail closed on indexed column keys before canonical ordering

predecessor_evidence.finding: Mixed exact-integer/non-integer indexed column keys could reach ordered.sort() before the relation-block boundary validated the column key, allowing Python tuple comparison to fail before the canonical fail-closed ValueError contract.

semantics: Materialize the existing indexed mapping once, as before.
Validate every row key as an exact int and within the existing row-axis bounds before sorting.
Validate every column key as an exact int and within the existing column-axis bounds before sorting.
Only after both indexed coordinates are admitted may canonical tuple ordering run.
Keep the existing TypedRelationBlock constructor as the final CSR, scalar, ordering and persisted-contract validator.
regressions: bool, float and string column aliases
mixed integer/string column keys that were previously incomparable during sorting
existing GPU-37 indexed row fail-closed regressions remain pinned

verification.note: This is pull-request integration evidence on the GitHub merge preview, not a claim that the full repository suite ran on the raw branch head.

claim_boundaries.correctness: The bounded indexed-column pre-sort admission defect reproduced by GPU-38 is fixed in the existing canonical indexed owner and covered by focused regressions.
